content.text: Barrington gives poor children Christmas gifts, then visits Owen’s home and sends him money. He leaves by train; Owen’s family waves from their front-room window. The text then contrasts capitalist poverty with socialism and includes Regulus’s Roman drama, in which he travels from Rome to Carthage despite certain death, defending honor and duty. Appendices describe Mugsborough. Later sections recount Elsie Inglis’s Scottish Women’s Hospitals: she works in Serbia, is taken prisoner, travels through Vienna and Zürich, then via Archangel, Moscow, Odessa, and Romania, treating wounded soldiers before returning to Newcastle, where she dies. Additional articles discuss inventions, mining, soap, nutrition, surveying, agriculture, technology, wildlife, and riddles.
